nodes.name: HE-O-MIEC green body preparation
nodes.procedure: MIEC precursors, including Li₂CO₃ (98%, Sinopharm Chemical Reagent Co. Ltd), Co₂O₃ (98%, Apinno), Pr₆O₁₁ (99.9%, Innochem), Nd₂O₃ (99.9%, Innochem), La₂O₃ (98%, Sinopharm Chemical Reagent Co. Ltd), BaCO₃ (98%, Sinopharm Chemical Reagent Co. Ltd), and SrCO₃ (98%, Sinopharm Chemical Reagent Co. Ltd), were mixed in a stoichiometric ratio. To compensate for the loss of Li, 10 wt % excess Li₂CO₃ was added. After ball milling for 6 hours with ethanol and ZrO₂ balls, the suspension was dried and pelletized in an oven at 80°C overnight. A green pellet of the MIEC precursors was pressed into pellets under cold isostatic (DJYP-100TZ) pressure at 230 MPa.

nodes.procedure: LLZTO (Hefei Kejing, China) powder was prepared by cold isostatic pressing at a pressure of 230 MPa and then sintered for 10 s by UHS technology to obtain dense LLZTO sheets.

nodes.procedure: B₂O₃ (Aladin, 99%) and Li₂CO₃ were initially mixed in a molar ratio of 1:2 and ground for 20 min in an agate mortar. The resulting mixture was subsequently heated in air at 600°C for 10 hours.

nodes.name: Cathode composite preparation
nodes.procedure: The obtained Li₃BO₃-Li₂CO₃ powders, HE-O-MIEC, and LCO were mixed in N-methyl-1,2-pyrrolidinone (NMP, 99%, Sigma-Aldrich) in a mass ratio of 15:20:65 to form a solid solution.

nodes.name: ASSLMB cathode sintering
nodes.procedure: The cathode composite was applied onto the dense LLZTO and the resulting double-layer structure. Then the double-layer structure was rapidly heat-treated for 3 s at 800°C using UHS technology to form a conformal cathode|LLZTO interface.

nodes.name: SPE Preparation
nodes.procedure: The precursor solution is composed of 1 M LiTFSI in a DEGA:FEC:HMPP ratio of 80:20:2 (v:v:v). FEC serves as a plasticizer and film-forming additive, while HMPP acts as the photoinitiator. Fifty microliters of the precursor solution was deposited onto the substrate and evenly distributed. The liquid precursor was then irradiated with an ultraviolet lamp (365 nm, 1100 mW cm⁻²) at a distance of 5 cm for 3 min, resulting in its transformation into a solidified polymer electrolyte.

nodes.characterization_summary: HE-O-MIEC synthesized at 1000°C exhibits a single-phase cubic perovskite structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: XRD results demonstrate that HE-O-MIEC synthesized at 1000°C exhibits a single-phase cubic perovskite structure (Fig. 3A).

nodes.characterization_summary: Nearest-neighbor distances measured at 0.277 nm and 0.396 nm consistent with (110) and (100) crystal plane spacing of perovskite oxides.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Under high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) (Fig. 3B), the nearest-neighbor distances in regions I and II were measured at 0.277 and 0.396 nm, respectively, which are consistent with the (110) and (100) crystal plane spacing of perovskite oxides.

nodes.characterization_summary: Relative density of HE-O-MIEC pellets was 98%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The relative density of HE-O-MIEC pellets was 98% using the Archimedes method (Fig. 3D).

nodes.characterization_summary: Elements are uniformly distributed with no observable secondary phases and elemental ratios correspond to the molecular formula.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM)/EDS analyses show that the elements are uniformly distributed with no observable secondary phases (figs. S9 and S10) and the elemental ratios closely correspond to the molecular formula (table S3).

nodes.characterization_summary: Homogeneous element distribution confirmed in an individual grain.
nodes.evidence_snippet: TEM/EDS further confirms the homogeneous element distribution in an individual grain (Fig. 3E).

nodes.characterization_summary: Co element in HE-O-MIEC present as +4 and +3 valence states with Co^{4+}/Co^{3+} ratio of 0.57.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) data suggest that the valence states of the Co element in HE-O-MIEC are present as +4 and +3, with a Co^{4+}/Co^{3+} ratio of 0.57 (fig. S11).

nodes.characterization_summary: Molecular composition confirmed as La:Pr:Nd:Ba:Sr = 1:1:1:1:1 and Li content of 0.09.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HRTEM/ energy-dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) and inductively coupled plasma (ICP) spectrometer analyses confirm that the molecular composition is La:Pr:Nd:Ba:Sr = 1:1:1:1:1 (tables S1 and S2).

nodes.characterization_summary: Electronic conductivity reaches 1150 S cm^{-1} at 25°C and decreases to 700 S cm^{-1} at 700°C, indicating metallic properties.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The electronic conductivity of HE-O-MIEC was measured at various temperatures using a four-probe technique. The electronic conductivity reaches 1150 S cm^{-1} at 25°C and decreases to 700 S cm^{-1} at 700°C, indicating distinct metallic properties (Fig. 4H).
